question: At which tested decoder blocks does transplanting one residual vector from a calendar edit change the preference for the next digit, holding the original prompt and answer prefix fixed?
selection: Include all four questions from the two previously observed pairs in which the same source edit restored one reference and lost the other. Test both original single-source replacements for each question, including the other calendar. This is a selected-case follow-up.
readout: At the final token of the supplied assistant prefix, read logit(3) minus logit(6). These are the first distinct tokens in 30 and 60. The shared trailing 0 is outside this readout.
intervention: For each input and site, align the edited donor and original receiver by the end of the same user content or supplied assistant prefix. Require the same token ID at both positions. At one decoder block at a time, replace the receiver output vector at this position with the donor output vector from the same block. All other positions retain their original computation at that block. Keep the receiver input IDs and positional encoding. Record prompt lengths and both site indices because the replacements may shift later positions.
controls: Read original and complete edited margins. For every receiver, block and site transplant the original vector back into its original run. Require absolute change at most 0.0001 log-odds. At the final block the prefix-final donor swap must reproduce the donor margin within 0.0001. A last-user-token swap at the final block must preserve the original margin within 0.0001.
report: Preserve all 24 block margins at both sites, both source edits and all four questions, including zero or opposite effects. Report any strict sign reversal, its first tested block and the range of measured changes. Contrast outcomes across both sites and sources. Repeat the complete experiment and compare saved reports. No generation, weight updates or model API requests.
limits: A single-position swap measures sensitivity to an artificial intervention conditional on this supplied prefix. The terminal prefix swap is an output-head control. A reversal cannot identify where information was first encoded, a unique path, or the model's reasoning.
